title: Past Continuous for Background Actions
grammar_goal: Enhances storytelling in Speaking Part 2 by creating atmosphere and showing the ability to combine complex tenses (Past Continuous + Past Simple).

core_rule.usage: Used to describe an action that was in progress at a specific time in the past, or a longer background action that was interrupted by a shorter, sudden event.

when_to_use: Speaking Part 2: Setting the scene for a story (e.g., 'The sun was shining and birds were singing when I suddenly heard a loud noise.').
Speaking Part 2: Describing an interrupted action ('I was walking to school when I saw my friend.').
when_not_to_use: Do not use for consecutive, completed actions in a sequence (e.g., 'I was waking up, was having breakfast, and was going to work' is wrong. Use Past Simple).
Do not use with stative verbs.

ielts_examples.writing: While the percentage of car owners was increasing, the use of public transport began to decline.
ielts_examples.speaking: I was studying for my final exams when my friend called to invite me to a concert.

repair_section.wrong: When I arrived, they had dinner.
repair_section.correct: When I arrived, they were having dinner.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: By the time I arrived, they were already in the middle of enjoying their evening meal.

repair_section.wrong: While I drove to work, I listened to a podcast.
repair_section.correct: While I was driving to work, I listened to a podcast.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: During my morning commute, while I was driving to the office, I listened to an educational podcast.

vietnamese_learner_mistakes: Overusing Past Continuous for main events in a story instead of background events.
Failing to match plural subjects with 'were' and singular subjects with 'was'.
Not using 'when' and 'while' correctly to link Past Continuous and Past Simple.

mini_sentence_repair_exercise.wrong_sentence: I read a book when the phone rang.
mini_sentence_repair_exercise.correct_sentence: I was reading a book when the phone rang.

mini_sentence_repair_exercise.wrong_sentence: While they was watching TV, the power went out.
mini_sentence_repair_exercise.correct_sentence: While they were watching TV, the power went out.

image_prompt_fallback: An illustration showing a person walking in a park (background action) and suddenly it starts raining (interruption). Text overlay: 'Past Continuous: Setting the Scene & Interruptions'.

quiz.question: Which combination of tenses correctly links a background action and an interruption?

options.A: While I cooked dinner, I was burning my hand.
options.B: While I was cooking dinner, I burned my hand.
options.C: While I was cooking dinner, I was burning my hand.
options.D: While I cooked dinner, I burned my hand.

quiz.explanation: 'Was cooking' represents the longer background action in progress (Past Continuous), and 'burned' represents the sudden, short interrupting event (Past Simple).
